scenario_description:
Objective: Keep tonight’s winter feedback-night lobby setup from narrowing the accessible entry path while preserving neutral check-in signage.
Emerging Need: Snow mats and a missing tabletop holder are harmless separately; risk appears when the wide folding easel is slated for the ramp-side mat lane before floor tape is set.
Decision Context: Stored supply notes identify the easel’s clearance constraint, acceptable alternate placements, and the facilities cutoff for reversible layout changes.
Consequence: Timely layout coordination can prevent a bottleneck before visitors arrive; after the footprints are locked, the entry may channel riders through an avoidable obstruction.

parameter.title: Winter rider feedback night lobby check-in
parameter.description: Neutral rider feedback table in Room B with volunteer check-in and wayfinding in the east lobby.
parameter.location: Harborview Senior Center Room B and east lobby

parameter.subject: Feedback night lobby mat note
parameter.body: Because of snow, absorbent mats are now down along the east-lobby ramp-side approach. Facilities will tape the check-in and sign footprints at 15:20 so the 17:00 entry line has a clear path. Noon diagram still pending.

parameter.content: Small tabletop sign holder isn’t in the outreach tote. I put the folding wayfinding easel from the Senior Center closet on the cart for tonight’s check-in so the welcome sign is visible.

parameter.subject: Feedback night floor-tape draft
parameter.body: Draft diagram places the coalition welcome easel beside the ramp-side snow-mat lane, aligned with the check-in table. Facilities has not taped it yet; final walk-through starts at 15:20.

parameter.subject: Feedback night floor tape locked
parameter.body: The 15:20 walk-through is complete. For crowd-control and insurance reasons, the east-lobby taped footprints and staged easel/table placements stay as marked until after the entry rush clears around 17:40.
